## Response

<!-- RESPONSE-START -->

A claim I have seen online is "drinking coffee late at night causes insomnia." Even though it sounds believeable, I am not sure it is completely true because most of the time I will drink coffee before bed because it helps me sleep. Therefore, I would use the principles of empiricism and control to design a study to test it. Empiricism means "relying on observation and measurement rather than personal opinion or assumptions." When I start this study, I would define the different variables in a clear and understandable way. First, "Coffee late at night" could mean drinking coffee after 7 p.m., and "insomnia" could be measured by the hours of sleep or how long it takes you to fall asleep after drinking the coffee. I would have the participants track their caffeine intake with a food diary and their sleep patterns using a device like a smartwatch to keep track of the data. After gathering the real evidence from my participants, I could start to see if there is a correlating relationship between drinking coffee later at night and sleep quality. Control is also important because many other factors can affect sleep, like stress, screen time, or how people react to caffeine. To make sure these factors don't affect my study, I could randomly assign participants into two groups: one that drinks coffee at night and one that drinks a caffeine-free drink. By keeping the other conditions the same, I would be able to figure out whether caffeine itself is causing the changes in sleep. Together, empiricism and control provide a more structured way to test the validity of these online claims. Instead of guessing, I would use a detailed and planned-out study with carefully managed conditions to find evidence that either supports or challenges the claim. <!-- RESPONSE-END -->

## Word Count & Range Check

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
get_response_text <- function() {
  f <- knitr::current_input()
  if (is.null(f) || !file.exists(f)) return("")
  x <- readLines(f, warn = FALSE)
  # Find the lines that EXACTLY match the start/end markers
  s <- grep("^<!-- RESPONSE-START -->$", x)
  e <- grep("^<!-- RESPONSE-END -->$", x)
  if (length(s) != 1 || length(e) != 1 || e <= s) return("")
  paste(x[(s + 1L):(e - 1L)], collapse = "\n")
}
count_words <- function(txt) {
  # Remove code blocks and inline code before counting
  txt <- gsub("```[\\s\\S]*?```", " ", txt, perl = TRUE)
  txt <- gsub("`[^`]*`", " ", txt, perl = TRUE)
  # Keep letters, numbers, spaces, hyphens, and apostrophes
  txt <- gsub("[^\\p{L}\\p{N}\\s'-]", " ", txt, perl = TRUE)
  # Split by whitespace and count non-empty words
  words <- unlist(strsplit(txt, "\\s+", perl = TRUE))
  words <- words[nzchar(words)]
  length(words)
}
txt <- get_response_text()
n <- count_words(txt)
minw <- as.integer(params$word_min)
maxw <- as.integer(params$word_max)
in_range <- n >= minw && n <= maxw
cat(sprintf("**Word count:** %d  \n", n))
cat(sprintf("**Required range (%s):** %d–%d words  \n",
            toupper(params$course), minw, maxw))
cat(if (in_range) "**Status:** ✅ In range\n" else "**Status:** ❌ Out of range\n")
```
